Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'Welcome,' says a quiet voice. 'Please wipe your feet. You are expected.'
Suggested line: 'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions. You are expected.'
Why: Restores the flagged 'wipe your opinions': Primm's polish in one clause, before he appears.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will no longer need to choose for themselves.'
Suggested line: All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier, and a little less themselves. I consider this the improvement.'
Why: Restores the flagged 'less themselves' beat in Primm's precise clipboard voice; also drops a stray second opening quote mid-note.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'When the champion is weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: he continues to train without the weights. Observe carefully.'
Suggested line: When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'
Why: Restores the story bible's own quote (precision that is accidentally funny) and drops a stray opening quote; the margin note then answers it.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see a curator patrol the side gallery, feather duster in hand. He straightens each frame without looking at its face. (A battle.)
Suggested line: A curator with a feather duster patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)
Why: Restores the flagged 'Anything alive, he dusts' and drops the 'You see' narration.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You face a clerk at a tall desk. His stamp falls rapidly; his eyes stay on the paper. (A battle.)
Suggested line: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)
Why: Restores 'Quite fast. Quite sad.' (flagged) while keeping the tested 'His eyes'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You face a vast staircase. Every step is the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
Suggested line: A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
Why: Restores the flagged image; 'You face a vast staircase' is placeholder narration.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You leave the cracked dome behind and return to the hall.
Suggested line: You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller. Most things here do. You go back.
Why: Gives the wing a closing image (his works shrink once looked at) instead of a bare exit line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You sit in the reading chair. One person has worn a hollow in its seat. Beside you, lamplight shines through a handmade shade.
Suggested line: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand. It is a little crooked.
Why: Puts back the flagged human detail and ends on 'crooked', the game's word for freedom, in Primm's own room.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You follow the lines of the plans with one finger. Then you roll up the best and take it. Your throat tightens.
Suggested line: They are good. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.
Why: Restores the flagged 'They are so good' motif: Primm began as a good man.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You remove the old gold frame. The mirror remains hanging; you can still see yourself. The gold will sell for a good price.
Suggested line: You prise off the old gold frame and leave the mirror hanging, bare. It still shows whoever stands in front of it. It never needed the gold.
Why: The current line reads like a receipt; this keeps the gold and lands the room's point.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find the brass collection plate bolted to the wall, marked for {villain_title}. You take the coins.
Suggested line: A little brass plate for donations to {villain_title}, bolted to the wall. It is quite full. You take the lot.
Why: Restores the flagged dry 'It is quite full' (token kept).

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You close your hand around the money and leave the empty plate.
Suggested line: It is, after all, other people's money. They would want it back.
Why: Restores the flagged wry justification; the current line just restates the action.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find a pot of coins on the top landing, left as a tip by the last climber. You rub your legs and pocket it.
Suggested line: At the top, a pot of coins sits on the landing: a tip left by the last person who made it. You rub your legs and pocket the coins.
Why: Restores 'the last person who made it', which says what 500 identical steps cost.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You keep reading. Page after page describes work that helped people.
Suggested line: It goes on. They are good. They are so good.
Why: Restores the flagged motif; 'Page after page describes work that helped people' tells instead of shows.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read the last plan twice. You recognise the care in it. You close the journal gently.
Suggested line: Once, he was exactly the person you would want running a kingdom. You close the last journal very gently.
Why: Restores the flagged line that makes Primm tragic before the Last Journal.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: I've walked a long way. Everyone I met was afraid of you.
Suggested line: Sorry. That's forest mud. I've walked a long way, and everyone I met on the way here was afraid of you.
Why: Restores the flagged first words to Primm: the Wanderer's own voice answering 'you have scuffed it'.

Speaker: Primm
Effective line: Every one of them has a number. I can account for every citizen. Nobody need be overlooked.
Suggested line: Every one of them has a number. Nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that?
Why: Restores Primm's flagged sincere, faintly proud question: numbering people as his gift.

Speaker: Primm
Effective line: Please remain still. I know how to put this right.
Suggested line: This will not hurt. It will, however, be Standard.
Why: Restores the flagged line: gracious, precise, and it names Phase 1 (Standardization).

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: People are different. You know that.
Suggested line: Because some things are five. Some people are.
Why: Restores the direct answer to 'Why must anything be five?' (flagged callback).

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Effective line: People are different. You know that.
Suggested line: Because some things are five. Some people are.
Why: Same callback in the rushed variant.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Suggested line: And nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Why: Restores Agnes's closing-line callback (story bible section 21) and keeps the tested phrase.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Suggested line: Nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Why: Same Agnes callback in the Necrocrat-only variant, where she was certainly heard.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
Effective line: You see Grandmaster Flex step from behind a pillar, unwinding a bandage from his arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
Suggested line: Grandmaster Flex steps out from behind a pillar, unwinding a very small bandage from a very large arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
Why: Restores the flagged image and drops 'You see'.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Effective line: You see the Grand Chef in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? Let me help.'
Suggested line: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No. Of course you have not.'
Why: Restores her flagged voice: she answers her own question, as only she can.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: 'The rules must answer for him too.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
Suggested line: 'It applies to him, dear. It applies to him very well.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
Why: Restores the flagged Agnes line (her technicality, with relish); rule text unchanged.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You stand among the pieces of the model. Tiny houses lie scattered across the floor. The table no longer holds a kingdom.
Suggested line: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
Why: Restores the flagged image: mess over perfection, the game's thesis in one sentence.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Effective line: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting go. I won't keep living in what you did.
Suggested line: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch.
Why: Restores the flagged answer: he shows Primm the letting-go instead of describing it (the earlier 'Watch how it's done' trimmed so it cannot read as a gloat).

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You hear the mirrors crack one by one. For the first time in ten years, {villain} sees himself in them.
Suggested line: The mirrors crack one by one, and for the first time in ten years {villain} sees himself in them.
Why: Drops the 'You hear' frame the earlier pass added; the image speaks for itself.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Above the small kingdom, you see a tired man kneeling without his crown or his perfect smile.
Suggested line: No crown. No perfect smile. Only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.
Why: Restores the flagged three-beat caption; the current one buries 'tired man' mid-sentence.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You stand in the light pouring through the broken glass.
Suggested line: Light pours in through the broken glass. It does not feel like winning. It feels like the end of a long, quiet lie.
Why: Restores the flagged 'end of a long, quiet lie' (the story bible quotes it), in present tense.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located!
Suggested line: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located! Please hold your applause until she has been removed.
Why: Plume's spin gets its turn: the slogan over the arrest.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Necrocrat wing's archive is filing from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
Suggested line: The Necrocrat wing's archive is paper from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
Why: Fixes 'is filing from floor to ceiling' (reads as a typo).

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. Fee is yours. Drink the tea while it is hot; freedom hasn't changed that part.'
Suggested line: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. The fee is still yours. The tea is not free just because the kingdom is.'
Why: Restores the flagged Hesper sting; the current line explains itself.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Waste of water when I could be watering the patch. Come back any time.
Suggested line: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Won't. Waste of good water. Come back any time.
Why: Same joke, half the words, in Fern's grumble.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: We visit every morning. I tell him about the people who helped us. I tell him about you.
Suggested line: We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.
Why: Restores the flagged Pell line; the current one repeats her intro ('every morning').

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: Flour on the ceiling. Food on the plates. Everything in its proper place, at last.
Suggested line: And chaotic. There is flour on the ceiling. I have never been so happy to have a mess.
Why: Restores the flagged line: 'everything in its proper place' is the regime's value, not liberation's.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: A hat of any size. I keep looking up, trying to decide.
Suggested line: I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two at once.
Why: Restores the flagged freed joy (One Approved Hat Size pays off with two).

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The bakery is painted on. We want a real one. None of us knows how to bake yet. Anyone can volunteer to be the first to burn a loaf.
Suggested line: The bakery is painted on. There is going to be a real one, as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. The recipe is: try.
Why: Restores the flagged punchline; the current line ends flat.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The hedge is round. I kept trimming the corners, and then I wondered why I wanted corners.
Suggested line: The hedge is round. The hedge wanted to be round. I asked it. I did not have to submit a form.
Why: Restores the flagged payoff to the square-hedge setup; giddy and specific.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Spontaneity every day! I don't know what comes next! I can hardly wait!
Suggested line: Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!
Why: Restores the flagged crooked joy; the current version is plain cheer.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: May I be honest? Your hat is awful. Thank you for wearing it.
Suggested line: I am not going to be polite today. I am going to be honest. Your hat is awful. I love it.
Why: Pays off her 'I am the politest person in the Showcase' setup (flagged).

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Any hat size is permitted. You may finally stop thinking about hat sizes.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain under review.
Why: Restores the flagged freed hat gag, still in broadcast voice.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity is no longer limited to Thursday. You may disregard this reminder.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise.
Why: Undoes the 'rehearse your surprise' setup directly (the voice bible's freed-announcement rule).

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank them.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank anyone who exists.
Why: Turns 'Please report anyone who exists' into its payoff.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
Effective line: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I keep almost asking permission to go for a walk.
Suggested line: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I thought I might go for a walk. If that is... No. I am not asking. I am telling you. I think.
Why: Shows the running gag (almost asking permission) instead of stating it.
